corpus.definition: A BOUND ROW is a data row of the table under "## Known upper bounds" or "## Known lower bounds", HTML comments stripped and the table header and separator rows excluded — the repo own definition, lifted from extract-pins.mjs so the audit and the generated pins count the same things. A CITED row names at least one bracketed reference token anywhere in the row; that token is what a reader follows, and this same list is the audit sampling frame.
corpus.partitionControl: WHAT THE CHECKS PROVE, narrowed twice by adversarial review on 2026-09-11 because the first two statements of it overstated. The partition (691 cited + 97 uncited = 788 bound as of 2026-09-27; 673 + 97 = 770 when this was written) proves only that the two classes EXHAUST the rows the parser enumerated; it cannot fail against real enumeration and is not evidence of completeness. Four narrow checks sit under it, each with a demonstrated failing case: the file inventory is checked against the mirror manifest own fileCount (round 2 showed a corpus of one intact file passing without it); every constant file must contribute at least one bound row; every section the committed generated pins expect must produce rows, which catches WHOLE-SECTION disappearance and nothing finer (round 2 drove 770/673 to 428/392 by renaming lower-bound headings while every file still contributed rows); and no line inside any bounds table BLOCK may fail to start with a pipe, which catches row loss within a section — every block in a section is walked, each block own header and separator excluded, and a blank line, blockquote, heading, HTML block or prose ends a block legally rather than being read as a lost row (round 3 stripped the optional leading pipe from 535 interior rows — legal GFM — and drove the corpus to 235/205 with every section still yielding its last row, so the pins and the section baseline both passed). A row that is well-formed, present, and simply absent from upstream is invisible to all of them, as it should be.
corpus.corpusControl: The 87a.md control A-47.note2 recorded reads 7 bound rows, 6 cited, carrying the string 857.5662 — identical under both the 2026-09-09 enumeration and this one. THAT IS THE WARNING, not the reassurance: the control passed under both while the totals differed by 130 rows, so a control that only asks whether a field is present cannot protect a number. corpus.baselineIndependence: RECORDED BECAUSE IT LIMITS THE SECTION CHECK: the per-section baseline is read from the generated pins in ledger/claims.json, which extract-pins.mjs cuts with the SAME section-matching code this counter uses. It therefore detects a section that stops parsing relative to the last committed snapshot; it is NOT an independent parser, and it would not notice a definition both programs share being wrong in the same way. That is why the table-syntax check exists beside it rather than inside it.
corpus.guardHistory: FOUR ROUNDS OF ADVERSARIAL REVIEW SHIPPED SEVEN FIXES INTO THIS DENOMINATOR AND ITS GUARDS ON ONE DAY, and three of the seven were defects in checks I had just written to fix the previous one. The pattern is worth more than any single fix: a completeness guard over a format I do not control is a parser, and a hand-rolled parser fails quietly in exactly the direction that flatters the number. What survives is narrow and stated: each check names the one failure it catches, the section baseline is explicitly NOT independent of the pins it reads, and the partition is described as exhausting the enumerated rows rather than proving completeness.
